questions.prompt: Which option is a fully managed (PaaS) relational database for new apps?

options.text: SQL Server on an Azure VM

questions.explanation: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed PaaS relational database (SQL Server engine) where Azure handles patching, backups, and high availability.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Azure SQL purchasing and options are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: vCore lets you size compute and storage independently
The serverless tier can auto-pause when idle
A new SQL server blocks all connections until you add a firewall rule
DTU lets you choose cores and storage completely separately

questions.explanation: vCore sizes compute and storage separately; serverless can auto-pause; new servers block connections until a firewall rule is added. DTU is a bundled model, not separate sizing.

questions.prompt: The purchasing model Microsoft generally recommends, where you size compute and storage separately, is ____.
questions.explanation: vCore lets you choose compute (cores + memory) and storage independently, supports serverless and Azure Hybrid Benefit, and is generally recommended.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to create and connect to an Azure SQL database.

items.text: Add a firewall rule for your IP

questions.explanation: Create the server, then the database, allow your client IP through the firewall, and finally connect and query.

questions.prompt: Match each option to its description.

pairs.right: Fully managed PaaS database for new apps
Managed instance with near-full SQL Server compatibility

questions.explanation: SQL Database is PaaS; Managed Instance is high-compatibility PaaS; SQL on a VM is IaaS; serverless auto-scales and pauses.
